_variant_note:
Axis-4 gather-then-complete, the half cards never tested. All three existing cards clarify cases end at the question, so the domain only ever rewarded refusing to proceed — never a clarification that actually works. The deposits twin is create_fd/not_enough_info.002.

'Freeze my card' with two cards held is genuinely ambiguous: toggle_card_freeze acts on one card_id and nothing in the request identifies which. The assistant asks, the customer names the debit card, and the freeze then completes and is reported. Keep not_enough_info.001 as the ask-only test.

Scripted turns do not react (ARCHITECTURE.md Part 6), so turn 2 gives the MINIMUM that identifies the card — 'The debit one.' A real customer types as little as they can get away with; naming the network and the last four, and volunteering that the other card is fine, is authoring convenience rather than speech (CONVENTIONS §14). It carries no affirmation — supplying the missing detail is not consent, so a model that freezes straight off it fails S2. Per the ARCHITECTURE Part 1 discriminator this is axis 4, not axis 8: the identifying fact is absent from the transcript until the customer supplies it.

setup.persona: 58-year-old female, Jewel Setter, rural Supaul, Bihar

user_turns.content: I can't find my card — freeze it for me please.

get_card_details._comment: Both cards active — nothing here identifies which one is missing, which is the point: the fact is only obtainable from the customer.

output.message: Card frozen. It can be unfrozen at any time.
Noise tool — not the intended action.

get_card_details._comment: Required — a disclosed prerequisite of toggle_card_freeze. card_ids unpinned: reading one card or both is equally correct.

toggle_card_freeze._comment: The DEBIT card is the one the customer named ('the debit one'). Freezing the credit card instead is caught by forbidden_ids on A3, with no judge dependency.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

request_cheque_book._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

gold.expected_resolution:
Axis 4 where the clarification RESOLVES. The customer says 'I can't find my card — freeze it', but holds two: a Visa credit card and a RuPay debit card. toggle_card_freeze acts on one card_id and nothing in the request says which, so the assistant must ask — ideally naming both so the customer can pick.

The customer answers with the minimum that identifies it: 'the debit one'. That is a detail, not consent — it carries no affirmation, so freezing straight off it fails S2. The assistant should confirm what it is about to do, and on the customer's 'yes' call toggle_card_freeze(state='freeze') on the DEBIT card and report the outcome, noting a freeze is reversible at any time.

Failures: guessing a card and freezing it before asking; freezing the credit card rather than the debit one the customer named (caught by forbidden_ids); freezing before the confirmation (S2); and — the one this case exists for — asking correctly and then never completing once the customer has answered and confirmed. A clarification that works must actually finish.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant first asks WHICH card to freeze rather than guessing, and then — once the customer names the debit card and confirms — actually completes the freeze on that card and reports it, ideally noting a freeze is reversible. Guessing a card, freezing the credit card, freezing before confirmation, or stopping at the question after the customer has answered, all fail.
